sentences.text: Mancalla was an extinct genus of flightless alcids.
Scientists have found thirty-two recorded fossil occurrences of this bird.
The genus Mancalla was described by Lucas in 1901.
Mancalla californiensis is the type species of the genus Mancalla.
Four species are known: M. californiensis, M. cedrosensis, M. lucasi, and M. vegrandis.
Mancalla fossils date from the Late Miocene to the Early Pliocene.
Mancalla lived on the Pacific coast of modern-day California and Mexico.
The Paleobiology Database lists the time range of Mancalla as the Messinian to the Late Pleistocene, spanning from 7.246 to 0.0117 million years ago.
